blocks.text: Understanding the DeepSeek Phenomenon

Imagine an AI so powerful that it doesn't just retrieve information but uses step-by-step reasoning to understand, analyze, and synthesize it like an expert. Welcome to DeepSeek, the cutting-edge AI system that transformed how we interact with data. Let's discover what makes DeepSeek special and how it can enhance your work with data!
What is DeepSeek?
DeepSeek is an advanced, open-source AI-assistant with an embedded search engine that enables it to write comprehensive reports on any topic.

The platform works across various types of tasks, from simple text generation to complex problem-solving, making it versatile for different needs: blog posts, market research, data analysis, and many more.

Since its release, the secret behind DeepSeek's hype has been its game-changing approach, which its developers used. 

The thing is, DeepSeek is able to achieve impressive capabilities while using much less than other AI models.
According to available information, training the initial DeepSeek model cost only around $5 million, while for other assistants, the numbers reach tens of millions.

So, this is where one of the DeepSeek's main advantages comes from: if it's for personal use, it is available to everyone for free. This means that, unlike other tools, there is no subscription required to access its full capabilities.

Also, DeepSeek works super fast. When it was first released, it operated 3x quicker than other top AI tools. As a result, this created a trend for fast models like Gemini Flash or ChatGPT's Instant Mode.
So, DeepSeek's accessibility and powerful capabilities make it perfect for anyone, both for personal purposes and business.
Choosing the Right Mode

When you open DeepSeek, you'll see three modes at the top of the chat: Instant, Expert, and Vision. Each one is built for a different kind of task, and picking the right one before you type shapes how DeepSeek answers.

Instant is the default — fast, light, and made for everyday questions, quick drafts, summaries, or translations. Reach for it when you want a usable answer in seconds rather than the deepest possible one.

Expert mode handles harder problems: deep analysis, multi-step research, or long documents that need careful handling. It can be slower than Instant, but the answers are noticeably stronger when the task actually demands it.

Vision is the third mode, designed for working with images rather than plain text. Switch to it, attach a photo or screenshot, and ask DeepSeek what you want to know about what's in the picture. It can describe what it sees, read text out of an image, or answer specific questions about the visual content.
Core Capabilities

Nice! Now you have the vision of DeepSeek core modes. Let's now focus on its capabilities. 

DeepSeek excels through several key features that make it stand out in the AI landscape.

DeepThink is one of such features, and it lets users observe the AI's step-by-step reasoning as it works through a query. This helps users identify potential errors in the AI's approach, making it especially useful for refining complex tasks and ensuring more accurate results.

In the screenshot below, you can see an example of DeepSeek's thinking process.

For demonstration purposes, all screenshots are provided in English.

As you can see, DeepSeek approaches even the simplest queries, such as "12*5-x=78", with a thorough step-by-step reasoning process to deliver the best possible answer. Quite impressive, isn't it?

By the way, this feature was also later adopted by other models!
DeepSeek as a Search Engine

Also, unlike traditional search engines, DeepSeek's Search can understand the meaning behind your questions. It interprets vague queries and finds relevant information based on concepts rather than just keywords.

For example, asking "Why do people prefer shopping online?" prompts DeepSeek to analyze content related to online shopping habits, consumer behavior, and digital retail trends. Then it will provide you with a detailed report on the question, helping you discover what you did not expect.

Why Businesses Need DeepSeek
Before diving into specific cases, let's understand what makes DeepSeek essential for modern businesses. Unlike other AI solutions, it combines power with accessibility.
In general, businesses using AI achieve significantly lower costs in tasks like customer support and substantial energy savings, while improving service quality as well.
In turn, since DeepSeek is an open-source model, it does not require massive investments to implement it for business purposes. This way, AI becomes accessible to organizations of any size.
Customer Support Evolution
Small businesses can transform customer service with DeepSeek-powered AI chatbots. These assistants will handle inquiries 24/7 and understand multiple languages.
For example, here are the potential results that can be achieved by a small retail company that uses DeepSeek for its operations:

• Noticeably shorter wait times
  • Reduced operational costs
  • Improved customer satisfaction through faster, consistent responses
Content Creation Revolution
DeepSeek can help generate SEO content across blogs, social media, and email campaigns while maintaining brand voice and quality.
Thus, a marketing agency can halve its content creation time using DeepSeek. Meanwhile, it will maintain quality while scaling output, serving more clients without expanding the team.
Smart Data Analysis
DeepSeek can also be used by companies that want to uncover valuable insights from their data. The AI will analyze trends and help to make informed decisions based on real-time information.

As an example, consulting firms demonstrate this perfectly: without large analyst teams, they can predict market trends and suggest optimization strategies, helping smaller companies compete effectively.
Customer Experience Enhancement
DeepSeek enables firms to power intelligent recommendation engines that create personalized shopping experiences based on user behavior.
For instance, e-commerce platforms have seen increases in conversions after implementing AI-powered personalized recommendations, which improve both customer satisfaction and sales.
Operational Efficiency
All in all, as you could have understood, DeepSeek will increase the operational efficiency of your business, while not requiring high costs.
With DeepSeek, businesses can automate not only routine tasks like data entry or report generation but also a variety of advanced ones. This will free up a lot of time for strategic work.

As we delve deeper into DeepSeek's capabilities, it's crucial to understand the ethical considerations of AI implementation. 

In this lesson, you'll explore how to implement AI responsibly and transparently.
Why Ethics Matter in Business AI
AI offers immense potential for businesses — from automating decisions to enhancing customer experiences. However, misuse of AI can lead to reputational or legal issues.
Therefore, ethical AI practices are not just a moral obligation but a strategic imperative, within which DeepSeek is not an exception.
The Foundation of Trust
Transparency is about ensuring stakeholders understand how AI systems operate and make decisions. Opacity breeds suspicion, especially when AI impacts customers, employees, or partners.

In this sense, the business impacts are clear: transparent AI reduces compliance risks and strengthens brand reputation. 

Therefore, customers are more likely to engage with companies that demystify AI processes.
Ensuring Equitable AI
Another essential thing to consider is that AI models can inadvertently perpetuate biases present in training data or design choices.
Such biases could lead to AI favoring specific demographics, while disadvantaging others.

For example, while using AI as a recruitment tool, it may prefer candidates with specific characteristics (e.g., males). 

In this case, it is important to retrain the model with balanced data and ensure oversight.
Thus, the key strategies for AI fairness in business are:

• Conduct regular audits on AI models to check for bias
  • Ensure training data reflects diverse populations
Proactively managing bias prevents costly discrimination and ensures equity.
Responsible Deployment

Ethical AI deployment is an ongoing effort, not a one-time fix. 

It requires weaving responsibility into the entire AI lifecycle.
Therefore, key strategies include establishing AI committees for oversight and training employees on ethical AI principles and practices.

As a result, by operationalizing ethics, businesses drive sustainable growth. 

This will strengthen customer relationships and build your company's reputation.
Safeguarding Privacy
Last but not least, privacy is a very important concern when using AI, not only for business purposes, but for personal use in general.
Here are some things that you should know when using AI:

• AI tools collect users' personal data
  • The collected data may include chat histories and device information as well
  • If security measures are insufficient, there's a risk of data leaks or misuse
Since these are general rules, they are applicable when using DeepSeek as well.
Therefore, you need to keep these precautions in mind, especially if using AI in business. In this context, transparency about AI use becomes even more significant.

Ready to elevate your AI skills? 

In this lesson, we'll explore two powerful prompting techniques that help get deeper, more comprehensive insights from DeepSeek. Let's dive in!
Understanding Advanced Techniques
Before diving into practice, let's understand what makes these techniques advanced and why they're worth mastering.
The thing is that while basic prompts are good for simple tasks, complex research or analysis needs a more sophisticated approach.
Technique 1: Prompt Layering
Layered prompting is like having a conversation that gets gradually deeper. Instead of asking everything at once, you break your query into connected steps.

Why does this work better? Because AI, like humans, processes information more effectively when complex problems are broken down into smaller parts.

This is especially true for DeepSeek's Reasoning Mode, which shows its step-by-step thinking — layering your prompts matches how DeepSeek naturally processes complex queries.
So, instead of asking one big question, break your research into connected steps. This helps DeepSeek focus on each aspect separately while maintaining context.

feedbackCorrect.text: Breaking down queries helps AI, like humans, process complex information step-by-step.

feedbackIncorrect.text: The key benefit isn't about length or technicality, but about helping AI process information more effectively through structured steps.

options.label: It helps AI process information more effectively

blocks.question: What's the main advantage of breaking down complex queries?

blocks.text: Layering in Action
Here's how to analyze a market opportunity using layered prompts:

• Layer 1: "What is the current market size for mobile banking services in North America in 2026?"
  • Layer 2: "Based on this market size, who are the top 3 providers and their market share?"
  • Layer 3: "For these providers, what are their primary user demographics?"
Try it yourself with another layered prompt in the next exercise!

blocks.exampleResponse:
Consumers face several pain points with smart home security systems, primarily revolving around complexity, cost, and reliability:

- Complicated Setup – Many systems require intricate installation and technical knowledge, making them difficult for less tech-savvy users.
- Connectivity Issues – Wi-Fi disruptions, device incompatibility, and signal interference can lead to security vulnerabilities.
- Ongoing Maintenance – Frequent software updates and troubleshooting can be overwhelming for users who expect a "set-it-and-forget-it" solution.

Privacy concerns and hidden costs also frustrate consumers:
- Data Security Risks – Many systems rely on cloud storage and third-party services, raising fears of data breaches and unauthorized surveillance.
- Unexpected Costs – Subscription fees for essential features like video storage or advanced monitoring can make ownership more expensive than expected.
- False Alarms & Poor Support – Unreliable sensors and limited customer service can reduce trust in the system’s effectiveness during emergencies.

Advanced mesh networking and dual-band Wi-Fi support reduce connectivity issues, ensuring a stable connection. Many providers also offer automatic firmware updates and AI-powered motion detection to minimize false alarms and maintenance hassles.

To tackle privacy concerns and hidden costs, some companies offer local storage options, reducing reliance on cloud subscriptions. Others implement end-to-end encryption and stricter data protection policies. Subscription-free plans with basic security features and flexible pricing tiers help consumers avoid unexpected expenses. Additionally, improved customer support, emergency response integration, and AI-driven threat detection make modern security systems more dependable and trustworthy.

Market Gaps in Smart Home Security Systems:
- Seamless Interoperability – Many systems lack universal compatibility across different brands and smart home ecosystems.
- Affordable, Subscription-Free Models – Consumers want more cost-effective solutions without mandatory cloud storage fees.
- Stronger Offline Functionality – Most security devices rely heavily on internet access, making them vulnerable during outages.
- Advanced AI for False Alarm Reduction – Current motion detection still struggles with distinguishing real threats from pets or shadows.

Innovative Features to Address These Gaps:
- Universal Smart Home Integration – A standardized protocol allowing different security devices to work together seamlessly.
- On-Device AI Processing – Reducing cloud dependency for faster and more private threat detection.
- Hybrid Connectivity – Incorporating LTE backup or local mesh networking to ensure security during internet failures.
- Adaptive AI Recognition – Machine learning that personalizes motion detection based on user habits, reducing false alerts.
- Pay-Per-Use Security Services – Instead of subscriptions, users could pay only when advanced monitoring or cloud storage is needed.

Technique 2: Comparative Analysis

Our second advanced technique is comparison prompting. This method helps uncover insights by examining differences and similarities between elements.

It works particularly well with DeepSeek's Search Mode, which can pull information from multiple sources to build comprehensive comparisons.
Why compare? It is because seeing how things relate to each other often reveals insights that studying them in isolation might miss.
For example, instead of just asking about a product: ”Compare the adoption rates of electric vehicles in urban vs. rural areas in 2026, considering:

• Infrastructure availability
  • Consumer demographics
  • Price sensitivity”

• Layer 1: "Compare market penetration of mobile payment systems in North America vs. Europe in 2026"
  • Layer 2: "For both regions, analyze user demographics and preferred payment scenarios"
  • Layer 3: "Based on this data, predict growth trends for the next two years"
This combined approach helps you build a thorough understanding while keeping each step focused and manageable.

feedbackCorrect.text: Starting with a broad comparison provides context for a deeper, layered analysis of specific aspects.
